newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE AT THE CROSSROADS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE AT THE CROSSROADS AGAIN.

text.p: Not for the first time, Paul Gascoigne has reached the crossroads.
But for the first time, the England midfielder, who turned 30 this week, has talked of quitting.
His future at Glasgow Rangers is uncertain although the club have offered him a new three-year contract and his place in the England team is no longer a foregone conclusion.

As he himself said on his birthday on Tuesday just four days before England face Poland in a decisive World cup qualifier in Chorzow: "If I'm picked, I'm picked. If I'm not, I'm not" although almost in the same breath he joked that all England needed to beat the Poles was him, and a goalkeeper.
But there were not too many other jokes as Gascoigne added another year on the line.
And he spelled out in no uncertain terms that the English news media may not have him to kick around much longer.
"People ask me if I will be able to play for another five years. If I keep getting hammered the way I am, then if I think I have had enough I will do what is best for me.

"If this goes on I could just walk away because there might be no fun left in football for me anymore. On the pitch I get slaughtered for whatever I do. People say I am too fat, and then, when I lose weight I am too thin.

"Then I should be beating five people, and, if I try it and lose the ball, then they say I shouldn't be trying that sort of thing. People say I should rise above the criticism and get on with my life but they're not the ones with a camera up their backside every minute of the day."
Gascoigne has been in the spotlight almost since he first made his Newcastle debut 12 years ago, displaying a natural ability that had not been seen in England for a generation.
Big money moves to Tottenham, Lazio and Rangers plus an irrepressible personality and a capacity for making headlines catapulted Gascoigne to star status.

The tears he shed during the World Cup semifinal against West Germany in 1990 created the "Gazza" industry, keeping journalists, advertisers, manufacturers, agents, lawyers and the paparazzi in business ever since.
The highs and lows of his career whether on or off the pitch make front and back page headlines.

"Away from the pitch its even worse," Gascoigne said on Tuesday, "I can cope with photographers following me around every hour of the day but when it starts on my family I can't take it. There is no way they should have to put up with it."
Many players have coped with the pressures and some have not, but Gascoigne's brilliance on the field at his best, comes from the same inner source that sparks the crazier side of his personality.

Talk to anyone who has ever shared a dressing room or a hotel with Gascoigne, and the stories come pouring out. Suits in the shower, shaving cream in socks, oranges belted through hotel windows, organising a busload of strangers intoa sing-song.
The other side of the coin is not so cheerful involving crassness, alleged wife-beating and stunts like burping into a TV microphone on his arrival in Italy to play with Lazio.
Still, the English cannot have it both ways. In Paul Gascoigne they had a talent that could have blossomed into one of the all time greats.
As he turns 30 the future is anything but certain.
